conventions.deviation_null: Στα αντικείμενα code_1/code_3 με kind="deviation", η τιμή null στο plus ή στο minus σημαίνει ότι η ΠΗΓΗ ΔΕΝ ΟΡΙΖΕΙ όριο προς εκείνη την κατεύθυνση (μονόπλευρη ανοχή). Είναι ΔΙΑΚΡΙΤΗ από το ρητό 0, το οποίο χρησιμοποιείται ΜΟΝΟ όταν το «0» είναι τυπωμένο αυτούσιο στην πηγή (π.χ. contact-02 «-0,+10» → minus:0). Καταναλωτής που βρίσκει null ΔΕΝ πρέπει να το ερμηνεύσει ως μηδενική ανοχή ούτε να απορρίψει αποκλίσεις προς εκείνη την κατεύθυνση· η παράμετρος απλώς δεν μετράται προς τα εκεί.
conventions.one_sided: Το προαιρετικό πεδίο one_sided σε μια γραμμή parameters δηλώνει ρητά ποια πλευρά μετράται ("minus" ή "plus") όταν η πηγή δίνει μονόπλευρο όριο χωρίς τυπωμένο 0.
conventions.general_criteria_preamble: Όπου η υποενότητα «1/ GENERAL CRITERIA» έχει εισαγωγική πρόταση στην πηγή (π.χ. «To fulfill the General criteria for T/O, SP:»), αυτή αποθηκεύεται ΑΥΤΟΥΣΙΑ ως ΠΡΩΤΟ στοιχείο του general_criteria με key="preamble" (ίδια σύμβαση με το contact-00-general). Δεν είναι κριτήριο βαθμολόγησης: καταναλωτής που απαριθμεί κριτήρια πρέπει να φιλτράρει το key="preamble". Το contact-06 ΔΕΝ έχει preamble γιατί η πηγή (σελ. PDF 30) δεν έχει εισαγωγική πρόταση εκεί.
conventions.lead_in_verbatim: Το lead_in_verbatim στο specific_criteria κρατά αυτούσια την εισαγωγική πρόταση του πίνακα (π.χ. «The following parameters are set as specific criteria for T/O execution:»). Ονοματοδοσία ευθυγραμμισμένη με το criteria_contact_c.json. Απουσία του πεδίου = η πηγή δεν έχει εισαγωγική πρόταση (π.χ. contact-07, σελ. PDF 31, όπου ο πίνακας ακολουθεί αμέσως το «2/ SPECIFIC CRITERIA»).
conventions.cross_ref_targets: Ο πίνακας cross_ref_targets είναι ΠΑΡΑΛΛΗΛΟΣ (ίδιο μήκος, ίδια σειρά) με τον cross_refs και δίνει τον μηχαναγνώσιμο στόχο κάθε παραπομπής (id item) ή null όταν ο στόχος δεν αναλύεται μονοσήμαντα. Ο cross_refs παραμένει πίνακας συμβολοσειρών, όπως σε όλα τα αρχεία του corpus.

items.name: GENERAL

general_criteria.text: The performance of SP in Basic Phase (Phase II) will be evaluated according to the following criteria, described below per category. For this purpose, the following rules apply:
The training program, the Performance Standards and the analysis of the Phase Training Units define the training pace. SP must have met the performance criteria by the end of the Training Phase.

Aircraft control must be smooth and solid. This means that a SP may meet the defined criteria for a maneuver - performance within limits - however, he/she may fail due to instability or negligence to precision or uncertainty.

Instantaneous, but not constant, deviations beyond the permissible “PLUS” or “MINUS” limits for altitude, airspeed, bank or other parameters are acceptable if immediate actions are taken by SP to correct them. Flight Safety must not be jeopardized and the instructor shall not need to prompt, intervene or take command of the Aircraft to restore smooth flight, throughout the maneuvering.
Knowledge and procedures application must be in accordance with the standardization of the relevant Manuals and instructions provided by Squadron, aiming at the efficacious mission implementation.

Specific maneuvers, intended to be solely demonstrated or performed during flight only, shall be separately cited on the remarks section of the grade sheet. When specific criteria are not mentioned for certain maneuvers, general criteria will be applied, along with criteria described in the Basic A/C Control standards.

Whenever IP’s intervention is required for completion of a maneuver being performed by SP, the latter will be graded with either “0” (minimum possible performance) or “D” (Dangerous handling of the aircraft).
Performance Criteria, upon which SPs are evaluated, are divided into General and Specific.

Evaluation of SP on the General criteria is carried out by Instructor Pilot (IP), based upon SP’s performance, in reference to the desirable performance criteria. Upon grading, IP is required to take into consideration both his estimation on SP’s experience and the relation between SP’s performance and the training section he/she is undergoing (according to IP’s judgment).

The performance of SP shall also be evaluated according to Specific criteria which define the deviations from the standard parameters of the maneuvers (altitude, airspeed, heading, etc.), as described below. These define the performance standards “1” and “3”, while the intermediate deviations define the performance code “2”.
Executing the maneuvers with deviations smaller than those mentioned at Specific criteria will be graded with “4”, whereas larger deviations will result in a “0” or “D” rating.
The maneuvers and procedures will be carried out during daylight and with VMC or IMC flight conditions, unless otherwise mentioned in the relevant criteria.
Criteria of the maneuvers performed under VMC flight conditions must be met in combination with spatial awareness control.

items.name: GROUND PROCEDURES
execution: To properly implement Ground Procedures, SP:
1/ Plans the mission suitably, according to A/C energy planning and his/her training level, taking into consideration all the data required for Mission planning.
2/ Informs the Instructor Pilot (IP) for any handicaps (if any) so far in his training.
3/ He/she takes part in or executes mission briefing according to the Mission Briefing Guide.
4/ SP must also be in a position to plan the alternative mission (when existing).
5/ Executes the normal procedures described in the Flight Manual, in the Local Area Procedures and in SOPs.
conditions: Upon Ground Procedures execution, the following Conditions apply:
1/ SP has the Flight Manual, Aeronautical maps, Guide Books, Navigation computer and mission planning sheets, at his/her disposal.
2/ Personal pilot equipment is provided for SP according to B.D.3-1/HATC.

general_criteria.text: To fulfill the General Criteria on Ground Procedures, SP:
Executes all checks according to check list, without IP’s intervention, in an impeccable and standardized manner.
Does not skip any procedure according to LAP and SOPs.
Cooperates with ground crew, without allowing mis-apprehensions.
Specifies the A/C condition and decides its flight permissibility correctly and confidently.
Is aware of ground crew’s position before activating any switch or move any A/C controls.
Follows specified taxi route and ensures that the ground path of the A/C is clear of obstacles.
Stops the A/C as required without oscillations and without IP’s intervention.
Does not allow any A/C movement when it should be halted (leak check, line-up, etc.).
Knows and uses correctly all A/C levers and switches.
Asks and waits answer from the instructor about the (BOTH) procedures.

items.name: TAKE OFF
execution: To properly execute T/O, SP:
1/ Executes the departure, which includes:
a/ Performing of Lineup Check and After Takeoff Checklist.
b/ Brakes release until the acceleration of the A/C up to the standard climb airspeed.
c/ A/C performance checks in accordance with the calculated T/O data.
d/ L/G and flaps retraction.
e/ Acceleration of the A/C to the standard climb airspeed.
f/ During Touch and Go, from the moment when SP places PCL at MAΧ position, until the A/C accelerates up to the standard climb speed.
conditions: Upon take off execution, the following conditions apply:
1/ SP takes off from runway centerline.
2/ Wind parameters are within limits.

general_criteria.text: To fulfill the General criteria for T/O, SP:
Executes LINE UP checks without omissions.
During engine run-up, does not allow any movement of the A/C.
Maintains the A/C at the centerline during T/O.
Brings and maintains the A/C to the proper T/O attitude.
Executes T/O with the standard airspeed.
Brings the A/C at the proper climbing attitude and maintains it.
Cleans the A/C configuration without violating Speed limit.
Accelerates and maintains the proper climb airspeed.

items.name: BASIC A/C CONTROL
execution: On Basic A/C control, SP:
1/ Maintains positive and smooth A/C control taking into consideration the current flight conditions.
2/ Trims the A/C in detail during flight.
3/ Performs cross check.
conditions: Day only (VFR – VMC)

general_criteria.text: To fulfill the General criteria for Basic A/C Control, SP:
Handles the aileron, elevator and rudder trim correctly, with ease and without any difficulty, within the full airspeed range during all flight phases and maneuvers.
Uses all A/C levers and switches with ease, without any difficulty and/or faults.
Executes all actions and checks according to Flight Manual, Standard Operating Procedures and Local Area Procedures.
Maintains the A/C within operational limits.
Maintains throughout the flight the required distance from clouds in order to remain VFR.
Checks continuously the indications from control and performance instruments of the A/C and compares them with the A/C positioning in space.
Executes the corresponding corrections, depending on the exterior stimuli and the duration of A/C maneuvers in all the flight phases.
Timely locates erroneous readings from A/C instruments, informs IP (when in dual flight) and executes the corresponding procedures.
Does not skip any procedure.
Knows the position and use of all A/C levers and switches.

3/ Overshooting (Nose-low) Final Turn Stall and recovery.

general_criteria.text: To fulfill the General Criteria on Traffic Pattern Stalls, SP:
Flies the A/C into stall, according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual.
Executes recovery procedures with the appearance of first stall characteristics.
Does not allow the appearance of secondary stall. In such a case SP takes the appropriate action.
Does not exceed the airspeed limits of landing gear and flaps.

items.heading_verbatim: (24),(26),(28),(33) LANDING (FLAPS LDG - FLAPS UP - FLAPS Τ/Ο - ELP - AΟA)
execution: 1/ Landing is considered the phase between the beginning of the level off (round out to flare), up to the point where either the engine acceleration begins (Touch and Go) or the A/C vacates the RWY (Full stop).
2/ Starts gradual reduction to power and reduce the rate of descent in order to level-off the A/C and assume landing attitude.
3/ Brings the A/C to touchdown point, with the proper attitude.
4/ After touchdown, either decelerates the A/C until safe taxi speed and vacates the RWY (Full stop) or advances the throttle to take off (Touch and Go).
conditions: Day or night.

general_criteria.text: Directs A/C to the RWY centerline.
Executes timely the round out procedure in order to level off the A/C and assume landing attitude.
SP brings the A/C in touch with the RWY, as described in Flight Manuals.
After touchdown, decelerates to taxi speed by applying the standard procedure. During deceleration, SP avoids abrupt oscillations and vacates the RWY following the LAPs, without any deviations.
Prevents and /or recognizes the appearance of high flare, late and rapid Roundout, Porpoising, Floating, Ballooning, Bouncing or touch down the RWY with a Drift and reacts accordingly.
Applies proper crosswind controls. In case not proper crosswind controls are applied and the student is not within proper touchdown parameters, he/she executes a go-around.
Executes touchdown within the first 1/3 of runway length, in an ELP.

items.name: AIRMANSHIP
execution: SP shall demonstrate the following features of pilot’s characteristics that additionally play a major role in CRM development.

1/ Awareness/Judgment: Correlates and keeps track of what is happening on the ground, in own aircraft, and other flight members, and copes with any subsequent mission impact as a result of these happenings.
2/ Risk management/Decision making: SP assesses risk and makes appropriate decisions.
3/ Task prioritization/Saturation: SP is able to put an order on his tasks according their significance.
4/ Flexibility: Copes with rapidly changing situations or conditions, in-flight or on the ground, and adjust mission as needed, to obtain desired objectives.

5/ Capacity: Cognizant of how large a task loading he/she can cope with before becoming saturated, confused, or frustrated to the point that safety is jeopardized or the mission is rendered ineffective.
6/ Flight Discipline: Follows directives and carries out all required steps in a procedure in the proper order.
conditions: SP shall demonstrate the proper airmanship throughout the mission

general_criteria.text: To fulfill General Criteria for Airmanship, SP must:
Awareness/Judgment:

Demonstrate the ability to minimize the effects of adverse factors and capitalize on opportunities to avoid mission degradation. Factors to be considered may include, but are not limited to, such items as weather conditions, airspace and approach restrictions, high-density traffic, aircraft capabilities and limitations, and fuel conservation.
Performs all operational checks according to Check list, Techniques and Procedures Manual and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Maintains orientation during flight.
Is able to return to base (RTB) safely or deviate to the alternate airfield.

Continuously monitors Control and Performance Instruments of the A/C and crosschecks with the A/C position. Performs required corrections by prioritizing his/her task accordingly in reference with outside visual cues during maneuvering and throughout the flight

Adjusts the execution of the mission in relation with the available flight time, in order to take advantage in the most efficient way of the remaining fuel (taking into account the current weather conditions), as well as the assigned flight area.
Risk management/Decision making:
Accurately identifies contingencies and alternatives.
Properly gather all available data before arriving at final decision.
Clearly state decisions.
Provide rationale in taking decisions.
Realize actual or potential hazards effectively and regulate his/her flight correspondingly, in order to positively avoid them.
Task prioritization / saturation:
SP put tasks in order without missing anything significant or violating any rule.
SP is able to handle multitasks in sequence without dropping any task out.
His/her task management does not drive into a channelized attention situation.
Flexibility in taking the right decision:
Correctly assesses all possible factors bearing on the situation and selects the best course of action.
Makes correct decisions based on complete or incomplete knowledge of the situation, foresees the outcome(s) of present actions and modify those actions as necessary to obtain the best outcome.
Makes alternative choices if need be, in order to alleviate the working stress and enhance mission effectiveness.

Capacity: Never exceeds his/her capabilities to control the aircraft safely. Selects an alternative course of action, when needed, to reduce task loading and allow for effective mission accomplishment.
Flight Discipline:
Has complete knowledge of all rules and regulations regarding flight.
Carries out all duties with minimum IP’s supervision.

general_criteria.text: To fulfill the General Criteria on General Knowledge, SP must:
Knows in detail all exercises given as daily assignment.
Κnows in detail the Flight Manual, the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual, the AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 and the aeronautical publications (ΜAΙΡ, maps etc.).
Has knowledge of meteorological principles and be able to attend the morning meteorological briefing without problem.
Has aerodynamics knowledge, so as to be able to explain, theoretically, situations to be encountered during flight.
Knows airport traffic procedures and have sufficient knowledge in order to plan a flight.
Has knowledge of air medicine and flight physiology, so that he/she can interpret all the physiology conditions and flight effects to be encountered.
Be aware of both sea and land survival procedures and the rescue procedures from SAR means.

items.name: CRM
execution: 1/ Integrate CRM skills into briefings - debriefings in accordance with CRM training.
2/ Gradesheets contain the following CRM items (where applicable):
a/ Mission planning/briefing/debriefing.
b/ Communication.
c/ Airmanship and its subcategories.
3/ Some or all of the above items are graded on every sortie.
4/ Discuss particular areas for CRM development / improvement.
5/ Solicit comments when CRM enhances mission effectiveness and safety.
6/ Check (V) mark the “CRM box” after debriefing to complete the grade sheet.
conditions: 1/ During the briefing.
2/ Throughout the flight.
3/ During the debriefing.

general_criteria.text: SP understands when CRM enhances mission performance and flight safety.
SP uses the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight particular items.
SP uses CRM concept – at max extend- when planning maneuvers or when analyzing certain situations (i.e. emergencies, etc)

If SP performs lower than expected, consider his/her level of experience. Apply MIF on items regarding his/her weak area and note on the gradesheet. (ie, When SP messes up radio drill in a blind situation use the appropriate MIF scale respectively for grading his performance).
